title: Wave-Particle Duality and Quantum Measurement
text:
Quantum physics mandates that energy and matter exhibit both wave-like and particle-like properties, a concept known as wave-particle duality. Before measurement, quantum entities are often described by a wavefunction ($\psi$), which represents the probability amplitude of finding the particle in various states.

The Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle establishes fundamental limits on the precision with which certain pairs of physical variables, such as position and momentum, can be simultaneously known. This limitation is not due to faulty instruments but is inherent to the nature of quantum reality itself.

Measurement acts as a collapse mechanism. When an observation is made, the wavefunction instantaneously collapses from a superposition of possible states into a single, defined state with fixed properties.
